Revised assessment incorporating SLOOS: The FOMC statement still depicts a solid macro backdrop—strong labor markets, robust household spending, inflation near the symmetric 2% objective—and a gradualist hiking path with floor-system tools (IOER and ON RRP) keeping the effective funds rate within the 2.25–2.50% range. The Financial Stability Report already tempers this with elevated asset valuations, high corporate leverage (notably among lower-rated firms), and more fragile risk sentiment amid volatility.

SLOOS adds a clearer credit-channel headwind: banks reported weaker demand for construction and land development loans and tightened lending standards and other terms broadly, including for C&I and construction/land development across firm sizes. This combination of softer loan demand and tighter supply points to a cooling in credit-sensitive sectors (CRE, capex), reinforcing two-sided risks and a more guarded, data-dependent stance than the statement alone implies.

Net tone: constructive macro, but further tempered by tightening credit conditions and softer loan demand signaled by SLOOS.
